title: Contains Duplicate II
prompt: Given an integer array `nums` and an integer `k`, return `true` if there are two distinct indices `i` and `j` in the array such that `nums[i] == nums[j]` and the absolute difference between `i` and `j` is at most `k`.
hints: Checking every pair of equal values against the index gap is O(n^2) in the worst case — you can do it in one pass.
Maintain a sliding window of the last k indices as a hash set (or a map from value to most recent index).
For each index, first check if the value is already in the window set (a hit means a valid pair), then add the current value and evict the value that just fell outside the window of size k.

solution.approach: Slide a window of at most k+1 indices using a hash set. For each new element, check whether it's already present in the window — if so, a duplicate within distance k exists. Otherwise add it, and once the window would exceed size k+1, remove the element that just fell out of range from the left. This keeps the set's membership exactly matching the valid window at every step.
